issues.detail: The skill is tied to Next.js and the next-auth@beta v5 line, and the setup steps (proxy.ts, middleware, server actions) mostly don't carry over to the SvelteKit and Express frameworks that the description says it covers.

scenarios.name: github-login-with-avatar-header
scenarios.rationale: Both cover every rubric item (install commands, `auth.ts`, route handler, env vars, callback URL, server-component header with server actions), and B adds the next.config image setup, a name fallback and a clearer header component, while A adds a questionable maintenance-mode note and an unoptimized img tag.

scenarios.name: admin-role-credentials-nextjs16
scenarios.rationale: Response B follows the rubric closely: Credentials with JWT, Zod validation, the jwt/session/authorized callbacks, proxy.ts exporting auth as proxy, module augmentation, and a server-side auth() re-check. Response A switches to Better Auth and covers almost none of the Auth.js specifics, though it does mention proxy.ts and a server-side role check.

scenarios.name: drizzle-adapter-edge-split-config
scenarios.rationale: Both give the auth.config.ts / auth.ts split with the adapter, jwt strategy, and a proxy built from NextAuth(authConfig).auth; A explicitly states the edge instance can only verify the session cookie and cannot read the database, which the rubric requires, while B conveys this less directly (the proxy validates a signed cookie) and adds tangential edge-driver and Next 16 notes, and neither explicitly states the edge runtime can't open TCP connections.
